group.description: Whether a surface can actually be operated — by pointer, keyboard, and touch — including focus movement, dismissal, and acknowledgement of activation.

capabilities.title: Fully operable by keyboard
capabilities.description: Every action the surface offers can be reached and performed with the keyboard alone, with no pointer-only path to any capability.
capabilities.rationale: The evaluator exists and checks a real reachability property on the captured node rather than mere presence, so this is one of the few interaction capabilities provable today.

capabilities.title: Focus moves in a sensible order
capabilities.description: Sequential keyboard navigation visits elements in an order that matches their perceived reading order rather than their DOM accident.
capabilities.rationale: Direction-aware: in RTL locales the expected horizontal order reverses, which the reading-order claim type already documents but has never been exercised because the locale axis is unwired. `focus-order` has no evaluator yet.

capabilities.title: Modal surfaces contain focus
capabilities.description: While a modal surface is open, keyboard focus cannot escape to the inert content behind it, including through nested overlays.
capabilities.rationale: The library already ships useFocusTrap and FocusTrapPanel, so the behavior exists in code with nothing asserting it holds. Nested scopes are the case that breaks in practice.

capabilities.title: Focus returns where it came from
capabilities.description: When a transient surface closes, focus returns to the control that opened it, or to a deterministic fallback when that control no longer exists.
capabilities.rationale: Requires capturing before and after a close interaction rather than a single settled snapshot — the reconciler's one-shot capture model is the blocker, not the evidence channel.

capabilities.title: Escape dismisses one layer at a time
capabilities.description: The escape key closes the topmost eligible surface only, leaving surfaces beneath it open, and never dismisses a surface with unsaved work without warning.
capabilities.rationale: useEscapeKey exists in the library and its docstring already describes layering. Nothing verifies the layering under nesting, which is the only case where it matters.

capabilities.title: Nothing essential is hover-only
capabilities.description: Every affordance remains discoverable and operable when hover is unavailable, so no action is hidden behind a pointer capability the device lacks.
capabilities.rationale: DESIGN.md forbids hover-only affordances in every kit's Do-not list. The pointer axis needs engine work — the user-agent half exists, but the pointer and hover media features CSS actually keys off do not.

capabilities.title: Every gesture has a non-gesture path
capabilities.description: Swipe, drag, long-press, and pinch interactions each have an equivalent reachable through visible controls or the keyboard.
capabilities.rationale: Becomes load-bearing as soon as the manipulation assets (Draggable, Sortable, SwipeAction, Dismissible) exist. Checking the alternative exists is structural; checking the gesture itself works needs BAS ACTION_TYPE_GESTURE driven by the reconciler.

capabilities.title: Activation is acknowledged immediately
capabilities.description: A control that starts asynchronous work shows a busy state on the same interaction, prevents duplicate submission where duplication would be harmful, and returns to a usable state when the work ends.
capabilities.rationale: DESIGN.md states this as a requirement for every async control. The `pressed` value on the interaction-state axis has no press-and-hold action in BAS today, so this is blocked on the axis rather than on evidence.

capabilities.title: Destructive actions are separated and confirmed
capabilities.description: An irreversible action is visually distinct from routine actions, is not adjacent to the action a user performs most often, and requires an explicit second step or offers undo.
capabilities.rationale: Partly structural — separation and contrast are measurable — but whether a confirmation is proportionate to the consequence is a judgment, so the ceiling is manual.
